title: A Daisy from the Park
story: Chris pressed wildflowers on country walks, partly to give the walks a purpose. He carried a heavy book, tissue paper, and a pencil for names he could only guess. At home he checked a field guide before writing a label, because a wrong name had embarrassed him once. His niece asked if the dry flowers were sad. Chris said they were a record of where he had been, and he showed her a page from a windy cliff. She pressed a park daisy herself. The hobby stayed simple, but Chris grew patient, since the flowers needed weeks before they would not curl.

vocabulary.definition: Flowers growing on their own, not planted in a garden.
A name written so a specimen can be identified.
Able to wait without becoming cross.
Bend out of a flat shape.

quiz.question: Why did Chris check a field guide before writing a name?
options: A wrong name had embarrassed him once
His niece had hidden the pencil
The cliff page had no flowers on it
The guide told him not to press daisies
quiz.correctAnswer: A wrong name had embarrassed him once
quiz.explanation: He checked the field guide before writing a label because a wrong name had embarrassed him once.
quiz.supportingSentence: At home he checked a field guide before writing a label, because a wrong name had embarrassed him once.

quiz.question: What does the pencil for guessed names suggest?
options: He could already name every flower without help
He noted uncertain names instead of trusting a first guess
He used the pencil only to draw the cliff
He refused to carry any paper on the walk
quiz.correctAnswer: He noted uncertain names instead of trusting a first guess
quiz.explanation: He carries a pencil for names he can only guess, so those notes are provisional until he checks them.
quiz.supportingSentence: He carried a heavy book, tissue paper, and a pencil for names he could only guess.

quiz.question: How long did the flowers need before they would stay flat?
options: A single afternoon
Until the next country walk
Weeks, or they might curl
Only until his niece chose a daisy
quiz.explanation: The flowers needed weeks before they could be trusted not to curl.
quiz.supportingSentence: The hobby stayed simple, but Chris grew patient, since the flowers needed weeks before they would not curl.

quiz.question: What does the niece's daisy suggest?
options: She threw the heavy book away
She thought the dry flowers were only rubbish
She already owned a complete field guide
She wanted to try the hobby after hearing what the flowers meant
quiz.correctAnswer: She wanted to try the hobby after hearing what the flowers meant
quiz.explanation: After he shows her a page and calls the flowers a record of places, she presses a daisy herself.
quiz.supportingSentence: She pressed a park daisy herself.

quiz.question: What is a label in this story?
options: The name written for a flower after it has been checked
The heavy book used to press the flowers
A wrong turning on a country walk
A page torn from a newspaper
quiz.correctAnswer: The name written for a flower after it has been checked
quiz.explanation: He checks a guide before writing a label, so the label is the name he gives the flower.
quiz.supportingSentence: At home he checked a field guide before writing a label, because a wrong name had embarrassed him once.
